task_title: fix: Bloom index gateway skipping chunks with 1 log line
problem_statement: Loki's bloom index gateway exposes an endpoint that filters a set of chunk references down to those whose bloom filters match a query's line filters. The endpoint short-circuits any request whose start and end time bounds are equal, returning an empty response without consulting the underlying bloom filters. This shortcut is incorrect: a chunk containing a single log entry has identical start and end timestamps, so a filter request scoped to that chunk legitimately has equal time bounds. Whenever a query targets such a single-entry chunk, the gateway silently drops it, producing search results that are missing log lines which should have been returned. The endpoint must process these requests like any other non-inverted time range.
problem_statement_variant: When a log search in Loki targets a chunk that holds only a single log line, the bloom index incorrectly treats the request as empty and removes that chunk from the results. As a result, single-line chunks are missing from query responses even though they should match.
